title: Unit of Work
objectives: Explain the key ideas behind Unit of Work.

definition: Unit of Work is a core concept in .NET Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Unit of Work is
theory.body: Unit of Work describes the methods and patterns used within .NET Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Unit of Work is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Unit of Work matters
theory.body: Without Unit of Work, systems built with .NET Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Unit of Work works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Unit of Work follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Unit of Work.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Unit of Work
theory.body: Unit of Work offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
